record.paper_title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a proper smooth Hamiltonian on R^{2n} whose set A^P_H of regular aperiodic energy values is dense? The paper argues that the plug-based construction used to create isolated or zero-measure aperiodic levels is unlikely to produce such an example, because away from the constructed aperiodic set the surviving periodic orbits remain non-degenerate and stable, whereas a dense aperiodic set would force every energy level to have only degenerate periodic orbits.

evidence.quote: This method is unlikely to be applicable to the construction of a function H with a dense set APH .
On the other hand, for a system with a dense set APH every energy level must have only degenerate periodic orbits.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H:\mathbb{R}^{2n}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a proper smooth function (so that all sublevel sets $\{H\le c\}$ are compact), and equip $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with its standard symplectic form $\omega_0=\sum_{i=1}^n dp_i\wedge dq_i$. Let $X_H$ denote the Hamiltonian vector field defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega_0 = -dH$. A value $c\in\mathbb{R}$ is called regular if $dH\neq 0$ everywhere on the level set $\{H=c\}$. Define the aperiodic value set
$$\mathcal A^P_H = \{c\in\mathbb{R} : c \text{ is a regular value of } H \text{ and the flow of } X_H \text{ on } \{H=c\} \text{ has no periodic orbit}\}.$$
Question: Does there exist such a proper smooth Hamiltonian $H$ on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ (for some $n\ge 1$) for which $\mathcal A^P_H$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture and the size of the aperiodic regular-value set turn up only constructions producing isolated or measure-zero aperiodic sets (e.g., Ginzburg, M. Herman, Kerman, Ginzburg–Gürel) and the survey discussing this very question. No construction of a Hamiltonian on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with a dense set of regular aperiodic energy values appears in the literature, and almost-existence results suggest such examples would be highly nontrivial; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Very little is known about how large the set of regular energy values without periodic orbits can be.
status_evidence.claim: Survey explicitly poses the density question as open.

status_evidence.title: A C^2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample producing a single aperiodic regular level set.
status_evidence.claim: Known constructions yield isolated aperiodic levels, not dense ones.

status_evidence.title: Aperiodic Dynamical Systems (Notices AMS)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys plug constructions which create localized aperiodic behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Plug methods are unlikely to produce dense aperiodic sets.
